name: Arsenal Football Club

identity.playing_style: Arteta's Arsenal play a 4-3-3 in possession that becomes a compact 4-4-2 without the ball, with Saka doing more defensive work than most elite wingers. Build-up is flexible: midfielders alternately drop into the back line or show ahead of it so progression can be tailored to the opponent. The 2025/26 title was built on the division's best defence (27 goals conceded, 19 clean sheets, lowest xGA in Europe's top five leagues at ~0.7 per game) rather than on volume attacking (71 goals, 66.1 xG). With Zubimendi at the base, Rice was released as a box-crashing No. 8; Guimaraes' arrival adds a second press-resistant carrier on the right of the three.
principles: defensive solidity and set-piece efficiency first
buy established Premier League / top-five-league players in their prime (Konsa 28, Guimaraes 28, Eze 28, Gyokeres 28)
Hale End academy pathway (Saka, Nwaneri, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman)
long coaching continuity under Arteta since Dec 2019
trim fringe wages each summer (Trossard, Norgaard, Kiwior, Vieira, Jesus out in 2026)
identity.club_character: Fully owned by Kroenke Sports & Entertainment since the 2018 compulsory buy-out of minority shareholders; large global fanbase, 60k Emirates Stadium, intense London media environment. Pressure is now about converting a title-winning core into European success after the 2026 Champions League final defeat on penalties.
identity.ownership: private (Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, Stan and Josh Kroenke)
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented: fan protests against KSE in 2021 after the European Super League episode (approx. 2,000 supporters outside the Emirates); the Arsenal Supporters' Trust opposed the 2018 KSE takeover. In November 2025 the club and the Rwanda Development Board announced the end of the eight-year 'Visit Rwanda' sleeve sponsorship (approx. GBP 10m a year) at the close of 2025/26, after UN reports on Rwanda's support for M23 rebels in DR Congo prompted supporter protests (Gunners for Peace) and an AST survey in which 86% of members wanted the deal ended.
identity.wage_structure: hierarchical (top earners reported ~GBP 240-300k/week; 2026/27 wage bill reported ~GBP 244m, 2nd in the Premier League)
identity.transfer_policy: Prime-age, Premier-League-proven or top-five-league starters bought for high fees; heavy net spend (2026 summer: ~GBP 194.5m in vs ~GBP 39.6m out); loans used to develop academy players (Nwaneri to Dortmund, Setford loan); few buy-to-sell profits.
identity.injury_management_reputation: Publicly criticised: Arteta himself called 2025/26 'worse' for injuries, with long absences for Havertz (knee surgery, out until January), Saliba (ankle, then a long-term back problem), Odegaard (shoulder/knee), Timber and Calafiori. Saliba, Timber and Eze are all sidelined at the start of 2026/27.

strengths: Best defence in Europe's top five leagues in 2025/26: 27 goals conceded, 28.5 xGA (~0.7 per game), 19 clean sheets; Raya named best goalkeeper.

Midfield depth and press resistance: Zubimendi (3,001 PL mins, 5 goals) anchoring, Rice (3,099 mins, 4G/5A) as a box-arriving No. 8, plus the GBP 75m addition of Guimaraes and Odegaard/Merino/Eze as alternatives.
Centre-back depth after Konsa (GBP 51m+4m) and Hincapie's permanent deal: six senior CB options, allowing Arsenal to absorb Saliba's long-term absence.
Proven big-game pedigree: Premier League champions (85 pts, 7 clear), 5-1 aggregate win over holders Real Madrid in the UCL R16, Champions League finalists.
Coaching continuity: Arteta in post since December 2019 with a stable, well-drilled 4-3-3/4-4-2 structure and elite set-piece routines.
Clinical No. 9: Gyokeres converted 14 PL goals from 55 shots (25.5%), the best goals-to-shots ratio among Arsenal's top scorers.
weaknesses: Spread of goals is thin behind Gyokeres: only Saka and Eze (7 each) reached seven league goals, and 71 GF / 66 xG is modest for a champion; Trossard (6 assists, 5-6 goals) has left.

Chronic availability problems: Saliba (back), Timber (groin surgery) and Eze (calf) all out at the start of 2026/27; Havertz missed most of 2025/26 after knee surgery; Odegaard had shoulder/knee issues.
Right-back is unsettled: Timber injured, White described as 'a shadow' of his best, Mosquera/Konsa are converted CBs.
Penalty/knockout mental scar tissue: lost the UCL final and EFL Cup final in 2025/26 (Gabriel missed the decisive penalty in Budapest).
Ageing/prime-age recruitment (Guimaraes, Konsa, Eze, Gyokeres all 28) limits resale value and concentrates the wage bill (reported GBP 244m, 2nd in PL).
Left-wing output: Martinelli scored 1 PL goal in 2025/26 and is in the final year of his contract; Tzolis is unproven in the Premier League.

data_quality.notes: Coach, 2025/26 league table (85 pts, 26-7-5, 71-27), UCL final, cup results, draw opponents (home/away split) and the five permanent arrivals are source-verified via search snippets. Direct page fetches were blocked for every sports domain, so per-player apps/starts/minutes are null except Raya, Rice and Zubimendi; PL goals/assists come from end-of-season scorer lists. Squad list is the official 2026/27 squad-number release minus confirmed deadline-day exits (Jesus, Nwaneri, Setford, Vieira); Zinchenko's status is unconfirmed (listed for sale, no verified exit) and Havertz/Kepa/Rice/Zubimendi/Dowman shirt numbers were not in the retrieved snippet. Fabio Vieira destination conflicts between sources (Porto GBP 7.7m vs Hamburg). Fees converted GBP->EUR at ~1.16 (Guimaraes GBP 75m, Konsa GBP 51m+4m, Hincapie GBP 34.5m, Tzolis GBP 34m; Kiwior EUR 17m+5m; Trossard GBP 15.3-17m; Jesus GBP 8.6m initial; Norgaard GBP 7m); net spend from Sports Mole GBP 194.5m in / 39.6m out. Contract expiry years are null except Konsa (4-year deal to 2030) and Martinelli (2027). Ages computed from public dates of birth as of 2026-09-02. Position benchmarks left null: no per-90 data was retrievable. Possession % not found.
